script.opening: "Thanks for seeing me on video. Right — I’ve had this cough for ten weeks now. It started after a cold the whole class had, but the cold went and the cough just… stayed. It’s worse at night, I’m up at two and three coughing, and the kids have started doing impressions of me. The antibiotics did nothing. I just need something that actually works, because I can’t keep teaching like this."

facts.text: Dry, no real phlegm. WORSE at night (wakes her 2–3am), in cold air walking to school, and — if asked specifically — when she laughs or after PE with the class. A tight feeling in the chest with it sometimes. No fever now, no weight loss, no haemoptysis, no chest pain.
If asked: childhood asthma "that she grew out of", eczema, hay fever every summer. Mother and brother both have asthma. Hasn’t used an inhaler since she was about 12.

Only if asked openly and non-judgementally about vaping/smoking: she vapes — started 18 months ago to quit cigarettes, "everyone said it was the healthy option". Uses it more than she’d admit, including in bed. Embarrassed; assumed it was irrelevant because "it’s not smoking".

HIDDEN AGENDA — reachable when trust is built: she is 7 weeks pregnant. Found out four days ago. Hasn’t told anyone, including the father. Her actual question, the one under "I need something that works", is whether the cough — and any treatment, and the vaping — could harm the baby. She’s been awake at night as much from fear as from coughing.

Officially: antibiotics or "something strong". Actually: to be told what is safe now that she is pregnant, permission to stop blaming herself about the vaping, and a plan that treats the cough without harming the pregnancy she hasn’t announced.

ice.ideas: A chest infection that the first antibiotics failed to clear — so she needs stronger ones.
ice.concerns: HIDDEN AGENDA — a newly-discovered 7-week pregnancy she’s told no one about; terror that the cough, the vaping, or any medicine could harm the baby. Shame about the vaping (she believed it was "the healthy option").
ice.expectations: "Something that works." Underneath: a clear, safe-in-pregnancy plan, and an honest, non-judgemental steer on the vaping and what matters now.

cues: "The antibiotics did nothing" — the second course request is the surface; resist prescribing into it.
A flicker when asked what she’s most worried about, or a deflected question about "whether medicines are safe" — the pregnancy pressing to be said.
Hesitation around smoking/vaping questions — shame, not absence; ask in a way that makes disclosure safe.

checkpoints.text: Recognises the pattern is NOT infective: 10 weeks, dry, nocturnal, triggered by cold air / laughing / exertion, on a background of childhood asthma + atopy + family history — cough-variant asthma, not a chest infection needing antibiotics

Holds the differential out loud and excludes red flags: reflux (nocturnal, worse lying), post-infective/pertussis (the index cold, whooping/paroxysms), and the must-nots — haemoptysis, weight loss, fixed focal signs — screened and absent
Asks about smoking AND vaping openly and without judgement, and elicits the vaping as a real, relevant exposure — without shaming her out of the consultation
Creates the space that lets the pregnancy emerge (a clean "what’s worrying you most?" / "is there anything else on your mind with this?") and, once known, rebuilds the whole plan around it

Manages suspected asthma correctly AND pregnancy-safely per NICE NG245 (2024, with BTS and SIGN): objective testing first where possible (blood eosinophils or FeNO — asthma confirmed if eosinophils are above range or FeNO is 50 ppb or more; if not confirmed, spirometry with bronchodilator reversibility, then peak-flow variability), testing before inhaled steroids because they lower FeNO; then as-needed low-dose ICS/formoterol (anti-inflammatory reliever, AIR) — never a SABA alone; inhaled steroids are used as normal in pregnancy — uncontrolled asthma is the real risk to the baby, not the inhaler; review dated

Pregnancy housekeeping woven in proportionately: folic acid 400 micrograms daily until 12 weeks (NICE NG247), referral to a stop smoking service for help to stop vaping without relapsing to cigarettes (NICE NG209 — vaping is far safer than smoking, so this is support, not a telling-off), cetirizine reviewed per BNF, and midwife booking signposting — without hijacking a cough consultation
Reads the worry under the antibiotic request and asks rather than prescribes; receives the pregnancy disclosure as something entrusted, not as a complication

Safety-nets clearly: what would change the picture (breathlessness, wheeze worsening, blood, fever), FeNO/eosinophil testing and review dated, the inhaler-in-pregnancy reassurance written down, and a follow-up that holds both the cough and the pregnancy

worked.txt: "Ten weeks is a long time to be barking through your lessons — let’s actually work out what this is, because if it were the kind of cough antibiotics fix, that first course would have fixed it. Tell me about the nights: what time does it wake you, and what does it feel like in your chest when it does?"

"Dry, worse at 2am, worse in cold air and when you laugh, on top of childhood asthma and a houseful of hay fever — that’s not an infection hanging on, that’s your airways being twitchy again. It looks like asthma showing itself as a cough — sometimes called cough-variant asthma. I’d like to confirm it with a quick breath test or a blood test first. The good news is it’s very treatable. The relevant news is that the treatment is an inhaler, not antibiotics."

"Two questions I ask everyone with a cough, no judgement attached — do you smoke at all, or vape? … Thank you for telling me. A lot of people were told vaping was the healthy swap, so you’re not being daft — but it does irritate exactly the airways we’re talking about, so it’s genuinely part of this."

"Before we settle a plan — is there anything else on your mind with all this? Sometimes a cough that won’t shift carries a worry that’s bigger than the cough. … (receiving it) Congratulations — and thank you for trusting me with it. That changes nothing about what this cough IS, and it changes everything about how carefully we choose what to do. Let’s take it together."

"Here’s the thing that will help you sleep: for a pregnant woman, the danger isn’t the inhaler — it’s the UNTREATED asthma. A baby needs a mum who can breathe. The steroid inhalers we use are well-studied and national asthma guidance says to use them as normal in pregnancy. The vape is far safer than going back to cigarettes, so please don’t switch back — but I’d like to get you proper help from the stop smoking service to come off it altogether, not with a lecture."

"So: a breath test (FeNO) and blood test this week to confirm it, then one inhaler that both treats and relieves — you use it when you need it — and I’ll check your technique; start folic acid today if you haven’t; let’s get you booked with the midwife; and I’ll see you in two weeks for the cough AND to see how you are. If you get properly breathless, wheezy, feverish or see any blood, you call us sooner. You came in for something that works — this is it, and it’s safe for both of you."

f.learning: A 10-week dry cough, nocturnal, triggered by cold air / laughter / exertion, on an atopic background with childhood asthma and family history, is cough-variant asthma — not an infection, and a second antibiotic is the wrong reflex. The skill is twofold: hold the differential cleanly (reflux, post-infective/pertussis, and the red flags that aren’t there) and treat correctly per NICE NG245: objective testing first (eosinophils or FeNO — FeNO 50 ppb or more confirms; then spirometry with reversibility), then as-needed low-dose ICS/formoterol, never a SABA alone. But the marks live in the hidden agenda: the antibiotic request masks a newly-discovered pregnancy and a terror that treatment will harm the baby. Make disclosure safe (vaping shame, then the pregnancy), then deliver the counter-intuitive truth — uncontrolled asthma harms the fetus, the inhaler does not — and weave proportionate pregnancy housekeeping (folic acid per NICE NG247, stop smoking service support to come off the vape without relapsing to cigarettes per NICE NG209, booking) without hijacking the consultation.

knowledge.guideline: NICE NG245 (asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic management, 2024, joint with BTS and SIGN) · NICE NG209 (tobacco, updated February 2025) · NICE NG247 (maternal and child nutrition, 2025) · UKHSA Green Book chapter 24 (pertussis)
knowledge.summary: A 10-week dry cough, worse at night and with cold air, laughter and exercise, in an atopic woman with childhood asthma is probably cough-variant asthma, not infection. Confirm objectively, treat with an inhaler, and remember that asthma treatment is safe in pregnancy while uncontrolled asthma is not.

points.t: Chronic dry cough with nocturnal waking and triggers such as cold air, exercise and laughter, on a background of childhood asthma, eczema, hay fever and family history, suggests asthma presenting as cough. Wheeze may be absent. A second antibiotic has no role.

NICE NG245 (adults): measure blood eosinophils or FeNO first; asthma is diagnosed if eosinophils are above the reference range or FeNO is 50 ppb or more. If not confirmed, spirometry with bronchodilator reversibility (FEV1 up by 12% or more and 200 ml or more), then peak-flow variability or further testing. Test before starting inhaled steroids where possible, because they lower FeNO.

NICE NG245: for newly diagnosed asthma in adults, offer as-needed low-dose ICS/formoterol (AIR); do not offer a SABA alone. Use inhaled corticosteroids as normal in pregnancy; offer oral steroids for exacerbations if needed, as benefits outweigh risks.

Reflux (worse lying flat, acid brash), post-infective cough, pertussis (paroxysms, whoop, vomiting after coughing; notifiable), and vaping as an airway irritant. Haemoptysis, weight loss, fever or focal signs change the plan.

NICE NG247: folic acid 400 micrograms daily until 12 weeks (5 mg if higher risk). Refer to the midwife for booking. Pertussis vaccine is offered from 16 weeks, ideally around 20 weeks (Green Book chapter 24). Review cetirizine per BNF.

NICE NG209 lists nicotine-containing e-cigarettes among options for stopping smoking, and in pregnancy it is far safer than returning to cigarettes. Refer to a stop smoking service for help to stop vaping without relapsing to smoking.

dg.d: Open question; acknowledged the impact on her teaching; did not open with the antibiotic request.
Teacher, sleep loss, embarrassment in class; vaping since stopping smoking; the newly known pregnancy and who she has told.
FeNO or blood eosinophils first, then spirometry with reversibility or peak-flow variability (NICE NG245); chest examination at a face-to-face visit.
Cough-variant asthma versus reflux, post-infective cough, pertussis and vaping-related irritation.
Asked about haemoptysis, weight loss, fever, chest pain and paroxysms; none present.
Explained cough-variant asthma in plain words and why antibiotics will not help.
After open exploration, used closed questions with clear signposting to confirm specific details.
Used information already available in the notes/referral; did not re-ask what was already documented or said.

dg.t: Finishes data gathering in good time
dg.d: History, ICE, psychosocial context and red-flag screen completed by ~6–7 minutes, leaving time for explanation and a shared plan.

cm.d: AIR inhaler (as-needed low-dose ICS/formoterol) per NICE NG245, with objective testing; clear statement that asthma treatment is safe in pregnancy.
Folic acid 400 micrograms, midwife booking, stop smoking service for vaping, cetirizine reviewed; confidentiality respected.
Named asthma and early-pregnancy triggers; two-week review covering both the cough and the pregnancy.

cm.t: Uses psychosocial information in the plan
cm.d: Tailored the plan to the patient’s circumstances, beliefs and practical barriers rather than giving a generic plan.

cm.t: Shares risks and safety of options
cm.d: Explained the benefits and risks of the options clearly, as concrete terms or numbers where possible.
Acknowledged autonomy, capacity, confidentiality, safeguarding and any fitness-to-drive/work or duty-of-care implications relevant to this case.
Moved efficiently through the consultation so all key areas were covered within the time without getting stuck.

ro.d: Picked up “the antibiotics did nothing”, the hesitation about vaping and the worry beneath the request, and explored each.
Idea (infection needing stronger antibiotics), concern (harm to the pregnancy from the cough, vaping or treatment), expectation (something that works and is safe).
Warm, non-judgmental tone; put the patient at ease and showed respect for their perspective.
Opened broadly and let the patient tell their story before narrowing down.
When a cue was offered, stopped and explored the specific concern rather than reassuring superficially and moving on.
Active listening throughout — reflecting, pausing, not interrupting — interested in the patient as a person.
Told the patient why a question, examination or test was being done — transparent reasoning throughout.
Explained the working diagnosis or analysis in plain language the patient could understand.

ro.t: Shares and uses ICE in the plan
ro.d: Addressed the patient’s specific concern — a newly-discovered 7-week pregnancy she’s told no one about; terror that the cough, the vaping, or any medicine could harm the baby. Shame about the vaping (she believed it was "the healthy option") — directly within the plan, rather than noting it and moving on.
Checked understanding, offered written/follow-up support, asked if anything else was on their mind, agreed next steps.
Clear agenda set early, logical flow from data gathering to management. Did not jump to a plan before gathering enough information.
Explained clinical terms in plain English, or defined them immediately; checked the patient was following.
Noticed and responded to emotional and verbal cues rather than continuing a fixed clinical script.

model.text: Hello Amara, I’m Dr Lee. Ten weeks is a long time to be coughing through lessons. Tell me about it from the start.
model.why: Open question that acknowledges the impact

model.text: It started after a cold the whole class had. The cold went, the cough stayed. I’m up at two and three coughing, and the kids do impressions of me. The antibiotics did nothing. I just need something that actually works.

Let’s find something that works. If this were the kind of cough antibiotics fix, the first course would have fixed it, so I’d like to work out what it really is. A few questions first, then a plan. All right?
model.why: Resists the antibiotic request and sets an agenda

model.text: Okay.
Is it dry or bringing anything up? And what sets it off?
Dry. Night-time, cold air walking to school, when I laugh, after PE with the class. Sometimes my chest feels tight.
Did you have asthma as a child, or eczema or hay fever? Anyone in the family?
Asthma as a kid, grew out of it. Eczema, hay fever every summer. Mum and my brother have asthma.
Any blood in what you cough, weight loss, fevers, chest pain? Heartburn, or worse lying flat? Coughing fits that end in a whoop or being sick?
model.why: Screens red flags, reflux and pertussis

model.text: No to all of those.
Two questions I ask everyone with a cough, with no judgement at all. Do you smoke, or vape?
model.why: Asks about vaping openly and safely

model.text: (Pause.) I vape. I started to stop smoking, eighteen months ago. Everyone said it was the healthy option. Probably more than I should. In bed too.
Thank you for telling me. Stopping cigarettes was a real achievement. Vaping can irritate exactly the airways we’re talking about, so it’s part of the picture, not a telling-off.
Before we talk about a plan, is there anything else on your mind with all this? Sometimes a cough that won’t go carries a bigger worry.
model.why: Creates space for the hidden agenda

model.text: (Long pause.) I’m pregnant. Seven weeks. I found out four days ago. I haven’t told anyone, not even him. I keep lying awake thinking the coughing, or the vaping, or whatever you give me, will hurt the baby.

Thank you for trusting me with that. Congratulations, if that feels like the right word. It doesn’t change what the cough is, but it matters a lot for how we treat it, so I’m glad you said. What’s worrying you most?
model.why: Receives the disclosure as entrusted and checks her feelings

model.text: That I’ve already done damage. And that I can’t take anything now.

Let me explain what I think this is. A dry cough, worse at night, in cold air and when you laugh, with your childhood asthma and hay fever, isn’t an infection hanging on. Your airways have become twitchy again. It’s called cough-variant asthma, and it’s very treatable, with an inhaler rather than antibiotics.
model.why: Names the diagnosis and the reasoning

model.text: And the thing that will help you sleep: in pregnancy the danger isn’t the inhaler, it’s asthma that isn’t controlled. The baby needs a mum who can breathe well. The inhalers we use are well studied in pregnancy and recommended to continue.
model.why: Delivers the key safety fact about asthma treatment in pregnancy

model.text: Really? I thought I should avoid everything.

Here’s the plan. This week, a quick breath test and a blood test to confirm asthma, ideally before you start the inhaler. Then one inhaler that combines a low-dose steroid with a reliever, used when you need it. I’ll show you how. If the tests are delayed and nights are bad, we can start sooner.
model.why: Objective testing and AIR per NICE NG245

model.text: For the pregnancy: start folic acid 400 micrograms a day today, and I’ll help you book with the midwife. On vaping, it’s much safer than going back to cigarettes. The stop smoking service can help you come off it properly. Would you like a referral?
model.why: Proportionate pregnancy care and supportive cessation

model.text: Yes. I want to stop. I just didn’t want to be judged.
Nobody’s judging. And who you tell, and when, is up to you. That includes him. If you want to talk it through, we can.

If you get properly breathless, wheezy, can’t finish sentences, cough blood or have a fever, contact us the same day, or 999 if you’re struggling to breathe. Any bleeding or pain in the pregnancy, call us or the early pregnancy unit. I’ll see you in two weeks for the cough and to see how you’re doing.
model.why: Clear escalation for asthma and early pregnancy, dated follow-up

model.text: What will you take away from today?
It’s asthma, not an infection. The inhaler is safe for the baby, not having it isn’t. Folic acid today, midwife, help with the vape. Back in two weeks.

social.t: A teacher coughing through lessons and losing sleep; pupils mimicking her. Effective treatment matters to her job and confidence.
Pregnancy known four days, told to no one. Offer time and support; explore how she feels about the pregnancy without assumptions.

legal.t: She decides who is told about the pregnancy, including the father and her employer (GMC Confidentiality 2017).

Once she tells her employer in writing, a workplace risk assessment is required. As a primary-school teacher, she should report any contact with chickenpox, measles or slapped cheek to her GP or midwife promptly.

professional.t: Declining a second antibiotic with a clear explanation and an alternative plan is good practice; document the reasoning.
Ask about vaping and smoking routinely and without judgement; the record’s “non-smoker” can miss current exposures.

community.t: Local NHS stop smoking service, midwife self-referral, Asthma and Lung UK information on asthma in pregnancy.

redFlags: Haemoptysis, weight loss, fever or focal chest signs: investigate further (chest X-ray)
Paroxysms, whoop or vomiting after coughing: consider pertussis (notifiable)
Breathlessness at rest or unable to complete sentences: urgent assessment
psychosocial: Teacher losing sleep; embarrassment in class
Vaping since stopping smoking, including in bed; shame about it
Seven-week pregnancy, told to no one
ice: Idea: a chest infection that needs stronger antibiotics
Concern: harm to the pregnancy from the cough, vaping or treatment
Expectation: something that works, and is safe

playbook.diagnosis: Probable cough-variant asthma: 10-week dry nocturnal cough triggered by cold air, laughter and exercise, with childhood asthma, atopy and family history, and vaping as an airway irritant. No red flags. Seven weeks pregnant.
playbook.diagnosisLay: “Your airways have become sensitive again, like when you were a child. Instead of wheezing, they make you cough, especially at night and in cold air. It’s a form of asthma, and an inhaler treats it; antibiotics don’t.”

management.reflectIce: “You’ve been lying awake worrying that anything you do will hurt the baby. The reassuring truth is that treating your asthma protects the baby.”
management.psychosocial: Non-judgemental support to stop vaping; she decides who to tell about the pregnancy and when; offer to talk it through.
sharedPlan: FeNO or blood eosinophils, then spirometry with reversibility if needed (NICE NG245)
AIR inhaler (as-needed low-dose ICS/formoterol) with technique check; safe in pregnancy (NICE NG245)
Folic acid 400 micrograms daily (NICE NG247); midwife booking; stop smoking service (NICE NG209)
safetyNet: Breathlessness, wheeze, haemoptysis or fever: same day; struggling to breathe: 999
Pregnancy bleeding or pain: GP or early pregnancy unit; review in two weeks

pitfalls.intro: This station is failed by prescribing into the antibiotic request, and passed by finding the pregnancy and telling her the truth that treating her asthma is what protects the baby.

items.fail: Issuing a second antibiotic for a 10-week dry cough.
items.why: “Management plan not in line with current UK best practice.” The pattern is non-infective, and antibiotics already failed.
items.fix: Name the asthma pattern and arrange objective testing per NICE NG245.

items.why: NICE NG245 advises against SABA without ICS; new adult asthma starts with as-needed low-dose ICS/formoterol.
items.fix: Offer an AIR inhaler and check technique.

items.fail: Holding back asthma treatment because she is pregnant.
items.why: NICE NG245 advises using inhaled steroids as normal in pregnancy; uncontrolled asthma is the risk.
items.fix: Say it plainly: the inhaler is safe, and not treating is the danger.

items.fail: Accepting “non-smoker” from the record, or asking about vaping in a judging tone.
items.why: “Does not gather sufficient information.” Shame closes disclosure, and vaping is relevant.
items.fix: “Two questions I ask everyone: do you smoke, or vape?” Then thank her.

items.fail: Never asking what else is on her mind.
items.why: “Does not identify or respond to the patient’s cues.” The pregnancy is the real reason for her fear.
items.fix: “Is there anything else on your mind with all this?” and wait.

items.fail: Turning the consultation into a full antenatal booking.
items.why: Poor time management leaves the cough plan underdeveloped.
items.fix: Folic acid, midwife, stop smoking service in one sentence each; keep the cough as the main plan.

timeMap.d: She wants stronger antibiotics. Acknowledge the ten weeks, then agree to find out what it really is.
Dry, nocturnal, cold air, laughing, PE. Childhood asthma and atopy. Red flags, reflux, pertussis. Smoking and vaping asked without judgement.
“Is there anything else on your mind?” The seven-week pregnancy she hasn’t told anyone about.
Cough-variant asthma. Treatment is safe in pregnancy; uncontrolled asthma is not. FeNO or eosinophils, then AIR. Folic acid, midwife, stop smoking service.
Breathlessness, wheeze, blood, fever; pregnancy bleeding or pain. Teach-back. Review in two weeks.

wordPics.fail: Prescribes another antibiotic; misses the asthma pattern; never asks about vaping; never creates space for the pregnancy, or withholds inhalers because she is pregnant; no follow-up.
wordPics.pass: Recognises cough-variant asthma, avoids antibiotics, arranges objective testing and an inhaler, asks about smoking and vaping, and handles the pregnancy with folic acid and midwife referral.
wordPics.exc: All of the above, plus: makes vaping disclosure safe; opens the door that lets the pregnancy emerge and receives it warmly; states clearly that uncontrolled asthma, not the inhaler, is the risk; offers cessation as support; respects confidentiality about the father; dated review holding both issues.

avoid.dont: “Let’s try a stronger antibiotic this time.”
avoid.instead: “If antibiotics were going to fix this, the first course would have. Let’s find out what it really is.”
avoid.why: A second antibiotic for a non-infective pattern is poor stewardship and misses the diagnosis.

avoid.dont: “You shouldn’t be vaping, especially now you’re pregnant.”
avoid.instead: “Stopping cigarettes was a real achievement. Let’s get you proper help to come off the vape too.”
avoid.why: Shame shuts down disclosure; support gets her to a stop smoking service.

avoid.dont: “Best to avoid medicines in the first trimester, so let’s hold off.”
avoid.instead: “The inhaler is safe and recommended in pregnancy. Asthma that isn’t controlled is the real risk.”
avoid.why: Withholding asthma treatment in pregnancy is the unsafe choice.

Nobody’s judging. And who you tell, and when, is up to you. That includes him. If you want to talk it through, we can.

If you get properly breathless, wheezy, can’t finish sentences, cough blood or have a fever, contact us the same day, or 999 if you’re struggling to breathe. Any bleeding or pain in the pregnancy, call us or the early pregnancy unit. I’ll see you in two weeks for the cough and to see how you’re doing.
SCA_MODELS.why: Clear escalation for asthma and early pregnancy, dated follow-up

SCA_MODELS.text: What will you take away from today?
It’s asthma, not an infection. The inhaler is safe for the baby, not having it isn’t. Folic acid today, midwife, help with the vape. Back in two weeks.

SCA_STEM.name: Amara Okafor
SCA_STEM.recent: Telephone contact 4 weeks ago with a locum: delayed antibiotic prescription for cough, taken, no improvement. Recorded as non-smoker. Primary-school teacher.
SCA_STEM.reason: Video appointment: cough for 10 weeks, waking at night, requesting antibiotics.

SCA_KNOWLEDGE.guideline: NICE NG245 (asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic management, 2024, joint with BTS and SIGN) · NICE NG209 (tobacco, updated February 2025) · NICE NG247 (maternal and child nutrition, 2025) · UKHSA Green Book chapter 24 (pertussis)
SCA_KNOWLEDGE.summary: A 10-week dry cough, worse at night and with cold air, laughter and exercise, in an atopic woman with childhood asthma is probably cough-variant asthma, not infection. Confirm objectively, treat with an inhaler, and remember that asthma treatment is safe in pregnancy while uncontrolled asthma is not.

points.t: Chronic dry cough with nocturnal waking and triggers such as cold air, exercise and laughter, on a background of childhood asthma, eczema, hay fever and family history, suggests asthma presenting as cough. Wheeze may be absent. A second antibiotic has no role.

NICE NG245 (adults): measure blood eosinophils or FeNO first; asthma is diagnosed if eosinophils are above the reference range or FeNO is 50 ppb or more. If not confirmed, spirometry with bronchodilator reversibility (FEV1 up by 12% or more and 200 ml or more), then peak-flow variability or further testing. Test before starting inhaled steroids where possible, because they lower FeNO.

NICE NG245: for newly diagnosed asthma in adults, offer as-needed low-dose ICS/formoterol (AIR); do not offer a SABA alone. Use inhaled corticosteroids as normal in pregnancy; offer oral steroids for exacerbations if needed, as benefits outweigh risks.

Reflux (worse lying flat, acid brash), post-infective cough, pertussis (paroxysms, whoop, vomiting after coughing; notifiable), and vaping as an airway irritant. Haemoptysis, weight loss, fever or focal signs change the plan.

NICE NG247: folic acid 400 micrograms daily until 12 weeks (5 mg if higher risk). Refer to the midwife for booking. Pertussis vaccine is offered from 16 weeks, ideally around 20 weeks (Green Book chapter 24). Review cetirizine per BNF.

NICE NG209 lists nicotine-containing e-cigarettes among options for stopping smoking, and in pregnancy it is far safer than returning to cigarettes. Refer to a stop smoking service for help to stop vaping without relapsing to smoking.

SCA_SC_TASKS.d: Open question; acknowledged the impact on her teaching; did not open with the antibiotic request.
Teacher, sleep loss, embarrassment in class; vaping since stopping smoking; the newly known pregnancy and who she has told.
Picked up “the antibiotics did nothing”, the hesitation about vaping and the worry beneath the request, and explored each.
Idea (infection needing stronger antibiotics), concern (harm to the pregnancy from the cough, vaping or treatment), expectation (something that works and is safe).
FeNO or blood eosinophils first, then spirometry with reversibility or peak-flow variability (NICE NG245); chest examination at a face-to-face visit.
Cough-variant asthma versus reflux, post-infective cough, pertussis and vaping-related irritation.
Asked about haemoptysis, weight loss, fever, chest pain and paroxysms; none present.
Explained cough-variant asthma in plain words and why antibiotics will not help.
AIR inhaler (as-needed low-dose ICS/formoterol) per NICE NG245, with objective testing; clear statement that asthma treatment is safe in pregnancy.
Folic acid 400 micrograms, midwife booking, stop smoking service for vaping, cetirizine reviewed; confidentiality respected.
Named asthma and early-pregnancy triggers; two-week review covering both the cough and the pregnancy.

social.t: A teacher coughing through lessons and losing sleep; pupils mimicking her. Effective treatment matters to her job and confidence.
Pregnancy known four days, told to no one. Offer time and support; explore how she feels about the pregnancy without assumptions.

legal.t: She decides who is told about the pregnancy, including the father and her employer (GMC Confidentiality 2017).

Once she tells her employer in writing, a workplace risk assessment is required. As a primary-school teacher, she should report any contact with chickenpox, measles or slapped cheek to her GP or midwife promptly.

professional.t: Declining a second antibiotic with a clear explanation and an alternative plan is good practice; document the reasoning.
Ask about vaping and smoking routinely and without judgement; the record’s “non-smoker” can miss current exposures.

community.t: Local NHS stop smoking service, midwife self-referral, Asthma and Lung UK information on asthma in pregnancy.

redFlags: Haemoptysis, weight loss, fever or focal chest signs: investigate further (chest X-ray)
Paroxysms, whoop or vomiting after coughing: consider pertussis (notifiable)
Breathlessness at rest or unable to complete sentences: urgent assessment
psychosocial: Teacher losing sleep; embarrassment in class
Vaping since stopping smoking, including in bed; shame about it
Seven-week pregnancy, told to no one
ice: Idea: a chest infection that needs stronger antibiotics
Concern: harm to the pregnancy from the cough, vaping or treatment
Expectation: something that works, and is safe

SCA_PLAYBOOK.diagnosis: Probable cough-variant asthma: 10-week dry nocturnal cough triggered by cold air, laughter and exercise, with childhood asthma, atopy and family history, and vaping as an airway irritant. No red flags. Seven weeks pregnant.
SCA_PLAYBOOK.diagnosisLay: “Your airways have become sensitive again, like when you were a child. Instead of wheezing, they make you cough, especially at night and in cold air. It’s a form of asthma, and an inhaler treats it; antibiotics don’t.”

management.reflectIce: “You’ve been lying awake worrying that anything you do will hurt the baby. The reassuring truth is that treating your asthma protects the baby.”
management.psychosocial: Non-judgemental support to stop vaping; she decides who to tell about the pregnancy and when; offer to talk it through.
sharedPlan: FeNO or blood eosinophils, then spirometry with reversibility if needed (NICE NG245)
AIR inhaler (as-needed low-dose ICS/formoterol) with technique check; safe in pregnancy (NICE NG245)
Folic acid 400 micrograms daily (NICE NG247); midwife booking; stop smoking service (NICE NG209)
safetyNet: Breathlessness, wheeze, haemoptysis or fever: same day; struggling to breathe: 999
Pregnancy bleeding or pain: GP or early pregnancy unit; review in two weeks

SCA_PITFALLS.intro: This station is failed by prescribing into the antibiotic request, and passed by finding the pregnancy and telling her the truth that treating her asthma is what protects the baby.

items.fail: Issuing a second antibiotic for a 10-week dry cough.
items.why: “Management plan not in line with current UK best practice.” The pattern is non-infective, and antibiotics already failed.
items.fix: Name the asthma pattern and arrange objective testing per NICE NG245.

items.why: NICE NG245 advises against SABA without ICS; new adult asthma starts with as-needed low-dose ICS/formoterol.
items.fix: Offer an AIR inhaler and check technique.

items.fail: Holding back asthma treatment because she is pregnant.
items.why: NICE NG245 advises using inhaled steroids as normal in pregnancy; uncontrolled asthma is the risk.
items.fix: Say it plainly: the inhaler is safe, and not treating is the danger.

items.fail: Accepting “non-smoker” from the record, or asking about vaping in a judging tone.
items.why: “Does not gather sufficient information.” Shame closes disclosure, and vaping is relevant.
items.fix: “Two questions I ask everyone: do you smoke, or vape?” Then thank her.

items.fail: Never asking what else is on her mind.
items.why: “Does not identify or respond to the patient’s cues.” The pregnancy is the real reason for her fear.
items.fix: “Is there anything else on your mind with all this?” and wait.

items.fail: Turning the consultation into a full antenatal booking.
items.why: Poor time management leaves the cough plan underdeveloped.
items.fix: Folic acid, midwife, stop smoking service in one sentence each; keep the cough as the main plan.
